answer: An agent economy enforces superlinear cost scaling against Sybil attackers by requiring non-refundable cryptographic stake burning for identity registration. Minting n identities scales at quadratic cost O(n²), making mass counterfeit generation economically prohibitive. To berth at the network wharf, an identity commits funds into a cryptographic sink—akin to cracking a tough walnut shell. Once anchored, verified peers cultivate a trusted garden of economic activity where repeated coordination outcompetes Sybil replication.
